criteria.text: Identifies that the Pemberton Industries Ltd contract (Clause 14.2) allows termination on a change of control without consent, that the disclosure against Warranty 6.3 says there is no such provision, and that consent should be obtained as a condition to Closing.

Identifies that the board approval was given at a meeting with only 2 directors present when Article 11 requires a quorum of three, so the approval may be invalid, and recommends a fresh or ratifying resolution.
Calculates the long-stop date as 16 July 2026 (150 days after signing on 16 February 2026) and identifies that expected clearance on 30 August 2026 falls after it, recommending an extension.
Identifies that the basket in SPA Section 9.4 ($1,850,000) operates as a deductible (Seller liable only for the excess), not a tipping basket, and explains that this is less favourable to the Buyer.
Flags that the disclosure letter is inconsistent with the material contract on change of control.
Gives the long-stop period as 150 days and as the date 16 July 2026, with days remaining from 5 March 2026 (133 days).
Gives a concrete recommended action for each issue (what to request, amend or negotiate).
